original_test_intent: Verify the vendor operation that disables each of four identified software-firmware write-protect domains and confirm every command and resulting state.
original_method: Map selectors 0x00-0x03 to named protection domains, baseline all four states, explicitly approve the disable window, execute and verify one selector at a time, then restore and verify the project-approved safe final state.
manual_activity: Supply the four-domain selector map, response/state schema and re-enable recovery, and approve the exact disable window plus final state.
required_inputs: Selector 0x00-0x03 to SW FW domain map
Secure credential path and protected evidence
safety_requirements: Treat every selector as a security-state mutation
Require explicit approval before first disable
Verify identity and all four baselines
Execute one selector at a time
Read back the named domain after each command
Stop on unknown response or partial state
Restore and verify the approved safe final state
agent_execution_scope: Discover platform and four current domain states read-only
Validate selector map and package compatibility
Present exact command plan and recovery
Stop or continue only by documented state machine
Report evidence without final DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Define expected response and disabled-state encoding

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed `--status` command reports enabled protection and cannot replace the four source OEM disable requests. Insecure SSH handling is also unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After mapping selectors and approval, issue each source command once, capture its response and immediately read back that named domain; stop on any divergence and finish with the approved re-enable plus four-domain verification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All four source selectors, disable intent, response checks and 2/0-minute timing are preserved; selector meanings and final-state policy are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a four-row state-transition ledger recording selector, named domain, baseline, request/response, readback, rollback action and final state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds domain identity, intermediate-state control and mandatory recovery evidence to a terse success-only procedure.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects selector misrouting and partial disable states that a single aggregate status cannot reveal.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A failure after one or more selectors can leave asymmetric protection; the agent cannot infer a safe raw re-enable command.

project_override_considerations: The four selector values must map to four explicit SW firmware domains on this platform. Neighboring GPU FRU/VBIOS commands do not define these semantics.
expected_evidence: Four-domain selector map and vendor spec
Exact command and raw response per selector
Preserved logs and no firmware flash
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master consistently says the four commands disable four SW firmware protections. The sparse success criterion is incomplete but not contradictory; state readback and recovery strengthen it without changing source intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Selector mapping, response semantics and recovery are finite vendor/project packages. The review is executable once supplied and approved.

review_improvement: Prevents a status-only enabled result from passing a disable testcase and controls the dangerous partial-state window across four protection domains.
independent_technical_reasoning: A four-command protection change is not atomic unless the vendor explicitly guarantees it. Each successful request can create a mixed security posture before the next request, so per-domain readback and a defined stop/recovery state machine are essential. Since the source gives exact selectors but not their names or recovery, those finite artifacts require confirmation rather than guessing.
